title: Surrounded Regions
statement_short: Given an m x n matrix board containing 'X' and 'O', capture all regions that are 4-directionally surrounded by 'X'. A region is captured by flipping all 'O's into 'X's in that surrounded region.
constraints: m == board.length, n == board[i].length, 1 <= m, n <= 200, board[i][j] is 'X' or 'O'
hint: Grid up to 200x200 permits O(m \* n) time by starting traversals from boundary 'O' cells to mark non-surrounded regions.
why_not: Right: Graph BFS starts from boundary 'O' cells, traversing connected un-capturable land cells into temporary markers before flipping remaining 'O's to 'X's in O(m \* n) time. Not Graph DFS: Recursive DFS works but can cause call-stack overflow on large grids. Not Union-Find: Disjoint sets link border nodes to dummy components in O(m \* n \* alpha(n)) time, but uses extra parent memory. Not 2D DP: Grid DP requires directional state flow, failing for 4-directional boundary component reachability.
complexity: O(m \* n) time, O(m \* n) space
